_comment: Every registry write is lock, re-read, change, save - Registry.mutate, directly or through tracking. The CLI's flash add-prompt, add-mcu's adoption and add-type each wrote a registry they had read before a prompt, with no lock: an edit the panel made while the prompt waited was erased by the save, and the prompt and adoption writes skipped tracking's refusals, so a board could end up tracked under two types or an unprovisioned Roadrunner's flash UID could be persisted.

mutations.name: the flash add-prompt tracks through tracking, not an unlocked direct write
add-mcu adoption tracks through tracking, so a board tracked elsewhere is refused
mutations.replace:
with Registry.mutate(c.paths, "adopt") as writable:
                added = writable.add_declared_serial(args.type, dev.serial)

mutations.name: add-type writes under the registry lock
mutations.find:
with Registry.mutate(c.paths, f"add type {args.type}") as writable:
        writable.add_type(
            args.type,
            args.chipset,
            klipper_args=args.klipper_args,
            katapult_args=args.katapult_args,
            katapult_installed=not args.no_katapult,
            overwrite=True,
        )
mutations.replace:
if True:
        writable = reg
        writable.add_type(
            args.type,
            args.chipset,
            klipper_args=args.klipper_args,
            katapult_args=args.katapult_args,
            katapult_installed=not args.no_katapult,
            overwrite=True,
        )
        writable._save(c.paths)
